external_sampler.note: macOS getrusage ru_maxrss is bytes and measures this separate Python process, including executable/PCK hashing. Serialized samples are content size, not allocated RAM. Game RSS is sampled only from the child PID.

notes: RSS is sampled macOS ps resident size in KiB converted to bytes; not peak private footprint or a leak proof.
Interval CPU percent derives from cumulative ps CPU time divided by monotonic wall time; 100% is one logical CPU. ps-reported %CPU is retained separately and is not the interval measure.
Sampling spans startup, active gameplay, separate scene loads and shutdown. Use timestamps and engine stage timing to distinguish those phases.

collector_memory.frame_storage: Preallocated PackedFloat64Array time + interval columns and PackedByteArray flags
collector_memory.note: Packed payload size is exact; container headers, backing-capacity rounding, allocator alignment, dictionaries and runtime bookkeeping are not included. Serialized diagnostic size is a reproducible content-size measure, not actual allocated RAM. Percentile/CSV/JSON construction occurs after active sampling and may raise later whole-process RSS. No claim that RSS growth equals game-only allocations.

conditions.audio: Normal runtime audio enabled; unique settings file, default volumes.
conditions.fixed_fps_source: Launcher explicitly runs normal real-time mode without --fixed-fps; absence is not inferred from consumed engine args.

runtime.engine_monitor_note: TIME_PROCESS / TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS are interval maxima updated about once per second, not per-frame CPU costs; zero static allocation counters are unavailable in the release build.
limitations: Frame intervals are wall time between SceneTree process callbacks, including cap/VSync waits, fixture reset work and ordinary game save I/O. They are not CPU-only or GPU timings.

Input probes start at injected in-engine events scheduled near process-frame callbacks and end at the first frame_post_draw with a changed target transform. No pixel readback is performed. Physical device, OS event delivery, compositor and panel latency are excluded; input phase is not randomized.
Static allocator monitors are unavailable in release exports. Zero/unknown values are reported unavailable. Render memory is an engine estimate, not process RSS or total unified-memory use.

External RSS and CPU sampling plus this harness add overhead. Frame packed buffers are allocated before warmup; monitor/event/probe records accumulate during measurement. Exact packed bytes and serialized diagnostic sizes are reported, not falsely treated as complete allocator or process overhead. Normal game saves remain enabled.
Load times are in-process resource load, instantiation, ready callback and first rendered viewport timing. They exclude process startup and do not establish cold disk/cache or cold shader behavior.
This run describes only the recorded host, resolution, focus, cap and power conditions. Other hardware, physical controllers, touch hardware, battery life and thermal sustainability are unverified.

warmup.workload: Same continuous active fixture; no idle-only warmup. Measurement begins without resetting the current motion.

watchdog.native_focus_loss_policy: Immediate abort during warmup or measurement; focus restoration does not resume this run.
watchdog.policy: Production lifecycle remains enabled. Startup requires stable native focus; a later pause or stalled route fails instead of automatically resuming or counting a stale motion flag as active work.

workload.description: Prepared launch state and starting position are injected using model APIs. Subsequent ramp/ground walking, resize, boarding, and toast launch use production input/animation. Completion resets are explicit fixture events. This is not an ordinary-input completion test or a whole-campaign performance claim.
